answer: An agent economy can bind each identity to a refundable stake and require it to answer unpredictable, cross-checked tasks over time; validators randomly sample claims, and a proven duplicate identity or coordinated false report burns the stake and lowers future selection probability. Creating a crowd of Sybils therefore means locking capital for every raven, fable, or sonnet persona, while detected collusion can slash them all, making identity multiplication costlier than honest participation.
